en: gangjeong; traditional Korean sweet grain snack

examples.en: My grandmother made gangjeong for the holiday.

examples.ko: 이 강정은 너무 달지 않아서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like this gangjeong because it isn't too sweet.

examples.ko: 시장에서 맛있는 강정을 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a bag of tasty gangjeong at the market.
Do you have any gangjeong to eat with tea?
I wrapped the gift box of gangjeong nicely.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 먹던 강정 맛이 아직도 생각나요.
examples.en: I still remember the taste of the gangjeong I ate as a child.

explain: '닭강정'은 달콤매콤한 소스를 입힌 닭튀김이라서 전통 과자 강정과 달라요. 이름은 같아도 가게에서 '강정'만 말하면 보통 명절 과자를 떠올려요.
explain_en: '닭강정' is sweet-spicy fried chicken, a different food from the traditional snack. If you just say '강정' alone, most people think of the holiday snack.

examples.en: In the morning I eat yogurt with raisins in it.
Raisin bread is the tastiest.
I don't like the raisins in cookies.
Raisins are made by drying grapes.

examples.ko: 아이가 간식으로 건포도를 한 줌 먹었어요.
examples.en: The child ate a handful of raisins as a snack.
I put raisins and nuts in the cake.

explain: '건포도'는 '마를 건(乾)'과 '포도'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 같은 '건'이 들어간 말로 '건어물'이 있어요. 한국 사람은 빵, 시리얼, 샐러드에 넣어 먹는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: '건포도' combines '건' (dried) and '포도' (grape). The same '건' appears in '건어물' (dried seafood). Koreans often have it in bread, cereal, and salads.

examples.en: Soy-sauce marinated crab is called a rice thief.
Mixing rice into the marinated crab makes it tasty.

examples.ko: 게장은 간장으로 담그면 짭짤하고 양념으로 하면 매콤해요.
examples.en: Marinated crab is salty with soy sauce and spicy with seasoning.
I ate the marinated crab my mother made herself.

examples.ko: 게장을 먹고 나서 손에서 비린내가 났어요.
examples.en: After eating marinated crab my hands smelled fishy.
I ordered the marinated crab set meal at the restaurant.

explain: 게장은 게를 간장이나 양념에 절여서 먹는 반찬이에요. 간장으로 담근 것은 '간장게장', 매운 양념으로 한 것은 '양념게장'이라고 해요. 밥이 계속 들어가서 '밥도둑'이라는 별명이 있어요.
explain_en: 게장 is a side dish of crab cured in soy sauce or seasoning. The soy-sauce kind is '간장게장' and the spicy kind is '양념게장'. It has the nickname '밥도둑' (rice thief) because you keep eating more rice with it.

examples.ko: 국수 위에 달걀 지단을 고명으로 올려요.
examples.en: I put egg strips on top of the noodles as a garnish.
For tteokguk, you top it with seaweed and meat as garnish.

examples.ko: 고명을 예쁘게 올리면 음식이 더 맛있어 보여요.
examples.en: If you arrange the garnish nicely, the food looks tastier.
I sprinkled sesame seeds on the japchae as a garnish.

examples.ko: 고명 없이 먹어도 맛있지만 있으면 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: It tastes good without garnish, but it looks nicer with it.

examples.ko: 할머니는 대추를 꽃 모양 고명으로 만드셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother made jujubes into flower-shaped garnishes.

explain: 맛보다는 모양과 색을 살리려고 음식 위에 올리는 것을 말해요. 지단, 김가루, 깨, 실고추 같은 것이 있고 '고명을 올리다/얹다'라고 써요.
explain_en: It is what you put on top of a dish, mainly to add shape and color rather than flavor. Examples are egg strips, seaweed flakes, sesame and thread chili; you say '고명을 올리다' or '얹다'.

en: snow crab; wary crab; queen crab

examples.en: In winter, we go to the east coast to eat snow crab.
The meat in snow crab legs is sweet and tender.
Dad steamed snow crabs and served them to the family.

examples.ko: 대게는 값이 비싸서 특별한 날에 먹어요.
examples.en: Snow crab is expensive, so we eat it on special days.

examples.ko: 대게 껍데기에 밥을 비벼 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Mixing rice in the crab shell is delicious.
This restaurant is famous for its steamed snow crab.

explain: 몸통은 작고 다리가 긴 게로, 영덕 대게처럼 동해안 지역 이름과 함께 자주 말해요. '꽃게'와는 다른 게예요. '대개(usually)'와 소리가 비슷하지만 철자가 달라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is a crab with a small body and long legs, often mentioned with east-coast place names, as in Yeongdeok snow crab. It is a different crab from '꽃게'. It sounds similar to '대개' (usually) but is spelled differently, so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.en: The bread that was just baked is nice and hot.
Drinking the piping hot broth relaxes my body.
In winter, hot hotteok is the best.
I like that the floor of the heated room is nice and warm.
This movie is a brand-new release.
Please eat while the rice is still piping hot.

explain: '뜨겁다'는 데일 만큼 뜨거울 때 쓰고, '따끈따끈하다'는 먹거나 만지기 좋은 정도로 따뜻해서 기분이 좋을 때 써요. 갓 나온 빵이나 국물에 자주 어울려요. 새로 나온 소식이나 작품에도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: '뜨겁다' is hot enough to burn, while '따끈따끈하다' is pleasantly hot, just right to eat or touch. It suits freshly baked bread or soup. It is also used figuratively for brand-new news or works.

examples.ko: 마트에서 새 소시지 시식을 하고 있었어요.
examples.en: They were doing a tasting of new sausages at the mart.

examples.ko: 시식 코너에서 맛있는 만두를 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried some tasty dumplings at the sample corner.

examples.ko: 시식 행사는 오후 두 시부터 시작해요.
examples.en: The tasting event starts at two in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 시식 후에 마음에 들면 사 가세요.
examples.en: If you like it after tasting, please buy some.

examples.ko: 주말에는 시식으로 배를 채우는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: On weekends, some people fill their stomachs with samples.
I won a spot at the new product tasting event.

explain: 마트의 시식 코너가 가장 흔한 장면이에요. 보통 작은 접시나 이쑤시개로 조금만 줘요. '맛보다'는 어디서든 쓰지만, '시식'은 팔거나 평가할 음식을 먹어 볼 때 써요.
explain_en: The most common scene is a tasting corner at a mart, where you usually get a tiny portion on a small plate or a toothpick. '맛보다' can be used anywhere, but '시식' is for trying food that is being sold or evaluated.

examples.en: We get our rice on a tray in the school cafeteria.
I stood in line holding my tray.
This tray has five compartments.
If you buy a tray for kids, washing up is easy.

examples.ko: 식판 위에 반찬을 골고루 담아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put a bit of each side dish on the tray.
Please return your finished tray over there.

explain: 칸이 나뉜 쟁반 모양 그릇이에요. 학교나 회사 구내식당, 어린이집에서 흔히 보여요. 집에서 아이에게 밥을 줄 때도 써서 '아기 식판'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a tray-shaped dish with separate compartments, common in school and workplace cafeterias and daycare centers. At home it is also used for kids' meals, called '아기 식판'.

en: going hungry; on an empty stomach

examples.en: I've been starving since morning, so I have no energy.

examples.ko: 점심을 거르고 쫄쫄 굶은 채로 회의했어요.
examples.en: I skipped lunch and sat through the meeting starving.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 쫄쫄 굶으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Going hungry all day is bad for your health.

examples.ko: 쫄쫄 굶고 있는 강아지에게 밥을 줬어요.
examples.en: I gave food to the starving puppy.
I had no money, so I went hungry for two days.
I came without eating anything, so I'll eat a lot.

explain: 거의 '굶다'와 함께 써서 아무것도 못 먹고 계속 배고픈 상태를 나타내요. 같은 소리로 시작하는 '졸졸'(물 흐르는 모양, 따라다니는 모양)과 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with '굶다' to show being hungry for a long time with nothing to eat. Don't confuse it with '졸졸' (a trickling stream, or following closely), which is a different word.

examples.en: Frozen meat needs to be thawed.

examples.ko: 해동 시간이 길어서 아침에 꺼내 놨어요.
examples.en: Thawing takes a long time, so I took it out in the morning.
I tried the microwave's defrost function.
Cook it right after it's thawed.

examples.ko: 급속 해동은 맛을 떨어뜨릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Quick thawing can make food taste worse.
I didn't know how to thaw it, so I searched online.

explain: 음식 이야기에서 가장 많이 써요. 자연의 얼음이 녹는 일은 보통 '해빙'이라고 해요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '자연 해동', '급속 해동', '해동 시간'이에요.
explain_en: It is used most in talk about food. Ice melting in nature is usually called '해빙'. Common partners are '자연 해동', '급속 해동', and '해동 시간'.

examples.ko: 봄에는 길가의 꽃에서 향긋한 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: In spring the flowers by the road give off a fragrant smell.
The coffee smells so nice that I want it every morning.

examples.ko: 갓 구운 빵 냄새가 정말 향긋해요!
examples.en: The smell of freshly baked bread is really fragrant!
This soap smells nice and feels soft.
Once I steeped the tea, the room smelled fragrant.
I like the scent of mugwort spreading fragrantly.

explain: 좋은 냄새, 특히 꽃, 차, 과일, 풀 냄새에 써요. 고기 굽는 냄새나 참기름 냄새에는 보통 '고소하다'를 써요. 비슷한 '향기롭다'는 글에서 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes pleasant smells, especially flowers, tea, fruit, and grass. For the smell of grilled meat or sesame oil, '고소하다' is the usual word. The similar '향기롭다' is used more in writing.
